readings.title: The boardwalk after sunrise
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At Reed Marsh, photographers began leaving the boardwalk to get closer to nesting birds. Signs already asked visitors to stay on the path, but many said they could not see anything from it. Rangers installed a screened viewing point overlooking a frequently used feeding area. They also offered an early walk explaining why distance mattered during nesting. Reports of people entering the reeds declined. The reserve did not claim that a viewing point solved every disturbance problem. It continued recording visitor behaviour and closed a short section when birds nested unusually close to the walkway.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Counting what is easy to see
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A volunteer counted waterbirds from the same bench each Sunday. When the total fell during a foggy week, she worried that birds were leaving the marsh. Her coordinator asked her to record visibility as well as numbers. Later comparisons showed that fewer birds were usually recorded when distant water was hidden, even if nearby groups were similar in size. The volunteer kept the low counts instead of removing them, but attached notes about conditions. A record of what could be observed was more honest than treating every count as an exact measure of the entire population.

readings.title: A pond without a feeding station
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Visitors to a town pond enjoyed feeding ducks, and some assumed more food always meant healthier birds. A park worker explained that unsuitable food could accumulate and affect water quality. The park introduced a short display showing natural feeding behaviour and placed benches where people could watch it. It asked visitors to leave feeding to the birds themselves. Some families missed their old routine, so staff offered a simple observation sheet for children. The aim was to preserve an enjoyable visit while replacing an activity that created problems. The new activity required patience rather than a bag of food.

readings.title: The quiet value of reeds
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: When a lakeside path flooded, a resident suggested removing all the reeds to make the bank look tidier. A local guide explained that the reeds provided shelter and helped slow water near the shore. Clearing them would not necessarily solve the problem that had blocked the path's drain. The maintenance team repaired the drain and cut vegetation only where it obstructed access. A display later explained the separate decisions. The bank still looked less neat than a lawn, but visitors could understand why some rough-looking areas were being kept. Appearance was only one consideration in managing the shore.

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

A path through a wetland allows visitors to enjoy a place without walking over sensitive ground. Its value depends on how it is used. Quiet observation may reveal more wildlife than a hurried visit. Protecting nature sometimes requires us to change our behaviour rather than build something new.
translation.referenceAnswer: 穿过湿地的小径让游客不必踩踏脆弱的地面就能欣赏当地景色。它的价值取决于人们如何使用它。安静观察可能比匆忙游览发现更多野生动物。保护自然有时需要我们改变行为，而不是修建新的设施。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Discuss how a nature reserve can welcome visitors while protecting wildlife. Propose two visitor rules and explain their purpose.
writing.sampleAnswer: A nature reserve should welcome visitors in ways that protect the place they have come to enjoy. First, visitors should remain on marked paths, especially near nesting areas. This reduces damage to sensitive ground and keeps people at a reasonable distance from wildlife. Second, the reserve should ask visitors to observe quietly and avoid feeding animals. Signs should explain the reasons behind both rules. A sheltered viewing point and a short guided walk would provide enjoyable alternatives to approaching birds closely. Rangers could record where disturbance continues and adjust access when necessary. Protection is more likely to succeed when people understand what is at risk and can still have a rewarding visit within clear boundaries.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。
